I farm 7 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, so I will treat the full 7 mu as one wheat crop and then the same 7 mu as one maize crop after wheat harvest. I have farmed this land for 40 years, and with well irrigation I do not like to leave yield to chance. I start from what has worked in our area, then I adjust by field strength, water, and input cost. For wheat, I will push a little harder on nitrogen because wheat here responds well when I can water on time, but I will still hold phosphorus and potassium at levels that keep the rotation balanced. For maize, I will also feed it well, because if maize goes short of fertilizer in the jointing to big flare stage, the yield loss is hard to recover. I do not chase extreme input use, but I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk an empty ear or a thin wheat head. On 7 mu, I can still manage carefully with family labor and some hired help only if timing gets tight. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize, keep wheat under rotary tillage after maize, and keep maize under no-tillage or light residue seeding after wheat if conditions allow, because that saves time and moisture. With irrigation, pest control, and timely field work, I will aim for steady yield, not gambling on either very low cost or very high input.
